name: Electrically Assisted Bicycle
description: A two-wheeled ride whose electric motor can propel it and a 170-pound rider no faster than 20 mph on a paved, level surface. Montana has no class 1/2/3 system: the definition counts it as a bicycle, so it rides under bicycle law. Defined by Montana Code Annotated §61-8-102(7), and included in the definition of bicycle by §61-8-102(2).
restrictions: Two tandem wheels and an electric motor; the definition draws no line between a throttle and pedal assist
The motor can't propel it and a 170-pound rider faster than 20 mph on a paved, level surface
No motor wattage limit in the definition
No classes: a 28 mph pedal-assist (class 3) e-bike fails the 20 mph test and isn't an electrically assisted bicycle
A faster machine with pedals, a power source of at most 2 brake horsepower and a top speed of 30 mph is a moped instead
Counts as a bicycle under state law, with a bicycle's rights and duties
No driver's license, registration or insurance
Ridden wherever bicycles are allowed; federal land managers may still treat it as motorized on their trails
